author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A federal judge has ruled that the administration acted unlawfully by directing the Federal Emergency Management Agency to cut its workforce in half. U.S. District Judge Susan Illston said the Department of Homeland Security improperly took over FEMA’s authority over its personnel and steered the agency toward eliminating thousands of disaster-response jobs.

The late-Friday decision cited a federal law enacted after Hurricane Katrina that bars DHS from substantially reducing FEMA’s authorities, responsibilities or functions. Illston agreed with unions challenging the cuts that the department violated the law when it moved to stop FEMA from renewing temporary contracts for on-call reservists who respond to disasters.

The ruling does not yet impose a remedy or penalty. The judge said the scope of relief will be addressed separately next month after additional briefing. She also noted that FEMA projected staffing of 11,383 for the coming fiscal year, roughly half its prior level, without a documented basis for that number. FEMA, DHS and the largest federal-worker union did not immediately comment Saturday.
dek: The court found that Homeland Security overstepped FEMA’s control of its personnel; remedies will be considered separately next month.
headline: Federal judge rules plan to halve FEMA workforce unlawful
